findings.title: traceID dropped from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line
findings.body: The old logRequest appended a traceID field (from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)) to the completed-request log. That block is removed and the new log call m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) does not add a traceID. The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware's instrumentContext also does not add traceID (it only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID and uname). Plugin request logs therefore lose trace correlation, which is a user-visible regression for debugging. The traceID should be carried into the contextual attributes or appended here again.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no tests and the moved logging behaviour is untested
findings.body: This PR moves the plugin context attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) out of LoggerMiddleware and into a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, and changes LoggerMiddleware to log via FromContext. No test covers that the contextual attributes are attached for QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics, or that LoggerMiddleware's completed-request log picks them up. The only test touched is the renamed metrics test, which checks only metrics. A regression in the attribute set would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Undocumented ordering dependency: request log fields now depend on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running earlier
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware no longer adds pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID or uname itself. It relies on the contextual logger already being in the ctx, which requires ContextualLoggerMiddleware to be placed before LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares. If someone reorders the stack or omits the contextual middleware, the completed-request log silently loses these fields with no error. The removed MetricsMiddleware comment ('this middleware should live at the top of the middleware stack') is not restated for the new middleware, and neither NewContextualLoggerMiddleware nor NewLoggerMiddleware documents the requirement.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so recorded calls are lost
findings.body: FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), a new instance whose InfoLogs/WarnLogs/etc. are not connected to the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now writes 'Plugin Request Completed' via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so a test that injects a TestLogger and then inspects its InfoLogs will see nothing. Such assertions would fail or pass vacuously after this change. The fake should return the receiver (or share its recording state) so the contextual calls are observable.

findings.title: Stale test name after the rename
findings.body: The file was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and the type is now MetricsMiddleware, but the test is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware. The rename is incomplete and the test name now refers to a type that no longer exists.

findings.title: PR description says the contextual logger moved into LoggerMiddleware, but it is a separate middleware
findings.body: The PR description says the contextual logger was moved 'to the LoggerMiddleware'. In the code, the contextual logger is a new, separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware (this file), which is wired as its own entry in CreateMiddlewares. Anyone relying on the description when reviewing or reverting this change will be misled about where the behaviour lives.
